name: Galladoria
summary: The hollow under Hy Brasil where the roots of the titan Olcasgean end, guarded by everything his rot has grown.

facts.text: Shrouded Isles (2002) gave Hibernia Hy Brasil, the lost home of the Sylvan, who asked the realm for help against the Fomorians.
The Sylvan are bark-skinned folk of Hy Brasil's forests, allied with Hibernia's races against the ever-encroaching Fomorians.
Galladoria is region 191, Hibernia's epic dungeon; the realm raid's final is Olcasgean (level 87).

Its halls hold the Olcasar (stonemelders, tainters, deepstalkers, a spikelord, a belladonna), Uaimh diggers and delvers, spindlers, sporites, lurkers, bottom feeders, hypogean beasts and deep shrouders.
Every 25-45 seconds an untargetable 'Eyes Watching You' effect hangs over one random player for five seconds; it does nothing else.
At the waterfall bridge a voice announces intruders, a deep voice answers, and the four Corrupt Primals rise; Olcasgean wakes only when all four are dead.
In May 2003 Olcasgean was killed by 140 players after an attempt by 340 failed.
Bot chat calls Olcasgean a titan banished to World's End whose roots taint the isle. World's End is a real Hy Brasil zone (region 181); the banishment itself is Living Server lore.
Irish olc means 'evil, bad'; the rest of the name Olcasgean is unglossed (to verify). Uaimh is Irish for 'cave'; eas for 'waterfall'.

story:
The Sylvan say Hy Brasil was not always an island. Before the Fomorians, before the Tuatha, before anything with a name, the land was one great body, and the oldest thing in it was Olcasgean. They do not call him a god. They call him the Root. When the first Sylvan woke in the forests he was already old and already angry, and the forests drove him out to the end of the world, the place still called World's End. He went, but roots do not leave. They go down.

Galladoria is where they end. It is a hollow under the isle, wet and warm and breathing, where the titan's sap pools and goes bad. Everything that drinks it changes. The Olcasar are stone that learned to hate. The Uaimh were cave-folk until the cave began to tell them what to do. Spores bloom on the walls and spindlers breed in the dark, and some of the Sylvan who came down to cut the root never went home; their shades walk the halls still. Things in the deep have been given work: a mechanism that pumps the world's soul like a heart, a conservator that hoards it, a falls that guards the last door.

Beyond the falls is the sanctum, and in it the Root sleeps, kept by the four elements of the isle, turned to his service. When intruders reach the bridge the walls speak. Visitors swear the stone watches them on the way in, and they are not wrong: now and then an eye opens in the dark over one of them, looks, and closes again. The Sylvan only nod. He is tired, they say. He is not asleep.
legend: A hundred is enough if they listen; three hundred is not enough if they don't. Clear the halls in order and do not wake the deep things two at a time. At the bridge, kill the four primals and nothing else matters until they are dead: air first with spells, fire with healers ready, water when it comes back from its pool, earth after its four menders. Then he wakes, and he is two of him.

firstEntry: The walls are warm, and they are breathing.
Roots as thick as towers. Something drinks here.
You feel eyes in the stone.

loremaster.intro: Galladoria. The hollow at the end of the roots, under Hy Brasil. The Sylvan will tell you about the [Root] if you sit with them long enough. Everything down there has drunk his sap: the [Olcasar], the [Uaimh], the things that keep the [world soul]. And at the bottom, past the falls, the [four guardians].

topics.Root: Olcasgean, whom the forests drove out to World's End before the first songs. His roots went down instead of away. The Sylvan say he is tired. They do not say he is asleep.
topics.Olcasar: Stone that learned to hate. Their geomancer can tear a piece off himself and send it to fight, and call his fallen back up from the floor.
topics.Uaimh: The cave-folk. Uaimh is only the old word for a cave. Their lairmaster runs home when he is hurt, and he is worse at home.
topics.world soul: The sap of the isle, as the Sylvan see it. Down there a mechanism pumps it and a conservator hoards it, and both will spend it on you.
topics.four guardians: Air, water, fire and earth, the isle's own elements, turned to keep the Root's sleep. While one stands, he does not wake. When the last falls, he does.

book.title: What the Sylvan Told Us of the Root
pages: I asked the old Sylvan at Domnann why her people do not go down into Galladoria. She said they did. She said a hundred of her kin went down with axes to cut the Root where it ends, and the Root let them walk a long way in before it began to drink them. Some of them are still there, she said, and they are not unhappy. That is the worst of it. She did not say more, and I did not ask.

Of the Root itself: he was old when the forest was young, and the forest did not love him. It pushed him to the edge of the world and he went, and he has been there since, at World's End, thinking. His roots kept going. They run under the whole isle, the Sylvan say, and where they end they have made a hollow like a mouth, and the water that runs down into it does not come out clean.

The four that keep his sleep are the isle's own. Wind and water, fire and stone: they were the land's before they were his, and the Sylvan grieve for them as for kin gone wrong. When a stranger crosses the bridge they speak with one voice and say they will protect. Then the Root answers from beneath the falls, and he sounds very tired. Those who heard it say tired is not the same as weak.
